reason: The text demonstrates God's explicit desire for Jacob's welfare through direct promises: God tells Jacob 'I will do good with you' (וְאֵיטִיבָה עִמָּךְ, 32:9), and promises to multiply his descendants as numerous as the sand of the sea. Since Jacob is being renamed Israel (32:28) and is the patriarch whose descendants will become the Israelite people, God's care and blessing toward Jacob and his progeny establishes a pattern of divine beneficence toward what will become the Hebrew people. The narrative shows God actively protecting Jacob through dangerous circumstances and facilitating his reconciliation with Esau, further demonstrating divine concern for his welfare.
